title: Read Your Own Profile Update
description: A primary acknowledges a profile update. The next request reads an asynchronous replica and sees the old profile. Assuming no failover, which policy directly addresses read-after-write freshness?

options.text: Add more asynchronous replicas and choose one at random.
options.explanation: Additional replicas can spread reads but do not guarantee that the chosen replica has applied this write.

options.text: Sleep for 50 ms before every read.
options.explanation: Lag varies with load and failures. A fixed delay is not proof that the write has been applied.

options.text: Route this freshness-sensitive read to the same authoritative primary, or wait for a replica to reach the write's version.
options.explanation: The read must use a source known to contain the write. Primary routing or a verified replay position provides that link.

options.text: Treat the acknowledged write as failed and submit it again.
options.explanation: A stale replica read does not prove that the primary failed to commit the write; resubmission can create a second effect.
